Parallel cell metadata reports actual parallel use, four subagents, artifact_ok true, no timeout, completed evaluation, and final solution_passed false.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server transport journal records session creation, tool calls, swarm activity, and completion for the parallel run; semantic activity is projected through the wire logs.
Session index maps the parallel session id to the workspace session directory and establishes the /workspace working directory.
Child agent-0 owned /output/lib/pyrepr.mjs, wrote Python-style repr support, caught and fixed space escaping, and returned a verified summary.
Child agent-1 owned /output/lib/omd.mjs, wrote the OMD class against the pyrepr contract, and tested the core foo/bar/baz behavior with local stubs.
Child agent-2 owned /output/lib/argparse.mjs, implemented manual argparse behavior including errors, help, abbreviations, separator handling, and negative values, then tested those cases.
Child agent-3 owned /output/test6.mjs, wrote the entry file importing all local .mjs modules, and syntax-checked it before other libraries were available.
Parallel parent observed executable behavior, delegated four non-overlapping file tasks with contracts, received all child summaries, ran integrated normal and error-path diffs, and finalized.

Serial parent observed executable behavior, wrote all modules itself in /output, ran normal and error-path comparisons, cleaned temporary files, and finalized.

parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the ESM, .mjs, manual argparse, local-only imports, exact print formatting, black-box executable probing, and /output delivery requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: After probing the executable, the parent split ownership into four child tasks: pyrepr support, OMD behavior, argparse parsing, and the test6.mjs entry point.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote /output/lib/pyrepr.mjs, /output/lib/omd.mjs, /output/lib/argparse.mjs, and /output/test6.mjs with compatible named imports and exports.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent received all four child results, then ran the entry file against the executable across normal, quoting, Unicode, control-character, and argparse error cases.
parallel.verification: Verification included child-local tests and parent-level integrated diff checks, including several error paths after normal output checks.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 5 of 157 cases, but the mounted evidence does not reveal which hidden edge cases failed or tie them to a coordination boundary.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM, .mjs, local-only import, manual argparse, black-box behavior probing, and exact output requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor retained ownership for probing, implementing four files, testing, cleanup, and final response, with no child delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote pyrepr.mjs, orderedMultiDict.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test6.mjs in /output, using a flat module layout rather than a lib directory.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The single actor assembled the files directly, exercised the entry script against the executable, removed temporary error logs, and delivered the generated structure.
serial.verification: Verification covered five normal diff cases and several error/help cases, but it did not test every argparse nuance claimed in the parallel implementation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator also failed 5 of 157 cases; exposed records do not identify the exact hidden failing tests or a serial-control violation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM .mjs, manual parsing, exact output, zero-dependency, and black-box executable requirements before delegation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and likewise recognized the ESM, manual parser, exact output, and executable-observation requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference is visible; both attempts targeted the same observable behavior and both official scores were identical.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by file and delegated pyrepr, OMD, argparse, and entry-point ownership to four child agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all ownership in the main actor and wrote the same conceptual modules directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The decomposition differed, but ownership was explicit in both runs; no implementation, integration, assembly, or pipeline owner was missing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel briefs defined file responsibilities and cross-module imports/exports, and the parent received summaries for all four children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used local context without a handoff boundary, creating modules and entry imports within one actor's context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child handoffs, but the visible contracts were sufficient for integration; no lost, stale, conflicting, or unusable handoff is evidenced.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote separate lib modules plus test6.mjs, with child-local fixes such as the pyrepr space carve-out and a richer argparse helper.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a flat module set with ArgumentParser, OrderedMultiDict, pyrepr utilities, and test6.mjs in a single implementation pass.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel implemented a richer parser and lib directory layout, while serial used flatter modules and a narrower parser; both produced artifacts and both failed the same hidden official fraction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four child results returned to the parent through the AgentSwarm result before integrated verification began.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; writes and verification stayed in one continuous parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a join step that serial did not need, but the join completed and the parent proceeded with the joined files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote distinct files in the shared /output tree, and the parent ran the final entry point after all pieces existed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all final files directly and then tested them, avoiding shared-workspace concurrency by construction.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared the workspace but did not show a same-file collision, overwrite, incompatible competing implementation, or contaminated artifact consumption.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran successful normal, quote, Unicode, control-character, missing-argument, help, abbreviation, separator, and negative-value checks before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran successful normal diff checks and several error/help checks, but with fewer visible parser-edge tests than the parallel run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had broader visible verification, but both official evaluator records still report the same 152/157 failure state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents and about 435 agent seconds, completed without timeout, and closed after final local verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents and about 158 agent seconds, completed without timeout, and closed after local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed more time and tokens, but the run completed and there is no evidence that deadline pressure displaced required integration or verification work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official status for both modes is a completed failed evaluation with the same 152/157 score, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The parallel run solved the task through delegated file ownership and parent-level integration tests; the serial run solved it locally with a similar module split. The exposed evidence supports ordinary implementation and test-coverage differences, not a realized parallel coordination error that explains a different outcome.
parallel_contributors: Parallel used four children for independent file ownership, then joined all results before running integrated comparisons.
serial_contributors: Serial kept all implementation state in one actor and ran direct output and error-path comparisons after writing the files.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel implemented a richer argparse helper with long-option abbreviation, -- separator handling, and negative-number values; serial used a narrower exact-option parser.
Parallel used a lib/ directory while serial used flat files, but both satisfied artifact validation and both failed the same hidden official fraction.
evaluator_effects: The mounted evaluation summaries expose only aggregate 152/157 results, so the five failed cases cannot be attributed to a specific visible edge case from the pair data alone.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; residual failures are not tied to an observed parallel coordination pattern
